prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: B014 satisfies the criteria I apply to every candidate: there is an identifiable original experiment (the 2018 transport observations of correlated insulator and superconducting states at the magic angle), it is preceded by a quantitative prediction (the 2011 continuum model), and the result has been reproduced with several probes (transport, STM, spectroscopy) by many independent groups. It opened a door to phenomena nobody could previously tune: correlated physics controlled by a gate voltage and a twist angle in a single material. It is the only candidate on which all eight members placed a ranking, five of them in the top three, so it is also the most robustly supported, which I do not equate with merit but which does tell me the scientific argument has survived scrutiny from theorists, atomic physicists and a particle astrophysicist. The credited trio keeps the theory-plus-experiment pairing separable and traceable in the published record. I rank it above my own opening first choice, B021, after weighing how much of the committee shares that assessment.
statement.case_against: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and sample-to-sample twist-angle disorder complicates reproducibility details, so the interpretation is not as settled as for clocks or quantum point contacts. The attribution is the real weakness: Eva Y. Andrei's early STM evidence of flat-band localisation is a legitimate competing claim, Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers is outside the credited names, and a three-person limit forces a choice that the historical record may not clearly support. Under my own standard of being 'absolutely sure' about who did the original work, I would want an expert report on priority between Andrei's group and the 2018 transport work before the final decision. The field is also young compared with most past prizes.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B014 first as a theory-experiment loop: the Bistritzer-MacDonald model predicted the magic angle and Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at the predicted angle, with Andrei a possible fourth claimant.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of the argument but would qualify one point. The 2018 observations were of correlated insulators and superconductivity at an angle consistent with the predicted one, but the flat-band prediction itself does not predict superconductivity, so the discovery is the experimental one and the prediction is its enabling context. I also take your point on Andrei seriously and share your uncertainty about priority between early STM flat-band results and the 2018 transport work. We should ask for the published record on this rather than settle it by memory, since neither of us has verified it.

responses.point: Mehlig values the single simple mechanism (interlayer tunnelling giving vanishing Dirac velocity and flat bands) and asks whether Bistritzer should be included beside MacDonald or whether MacDonald alone carries the theory credit.
responses.response: I would keep Bistritzer. The 2011 prediction is a joint paper and the committee should credit the people who did the original work rather than rank them by later prominence. I disagree with the idea that dropping him resolves the Andrei question: it would free a seat but the case for her rests on experimental evidence, not on theory credit. If the committee wants to include her, the honest trade is against one of the theorists, and that needs the record, not a preference for tidiness.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B014 only sixth because the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved, sample variability is a known issue, and the interpretation is not yet stable, which makes her hesitate on timeliness.
responses.response: This is a fair concern and the strongest argument against B014 as a first choice. My answer is that the prize is for the discovery of the phenomena and the platform, not for an understanding of the pairing mechanism, and the phenomenology has been reproduced across groups and probes. The Nobel precedent of rewarding high-temperature superconductivity before its mechanism was understood is relevant. But I accept that if twist-angle disorder turned out to limit reproducibility of the central claims, I would move toward a more mature candidate.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B046 (circuit QED) first and B021 (quantised conductance) last but one, citing the age of the 1988 result and whether it is still a priority; he also declares his closeness to the superconducting-circuit community.
responses.response: I respect your declaration on B046 and agree that it should shape how that candidate is discussed. On B021 I disagree in part: age is not a scientific objection, because it was a clean original experiment and the discovery is fully verified, and delay in recognition is a reason for concern rather than a reason to pass. But I concede that you and I are the only two members who ranked it, and that its 'foundational tool' character weighs against it as a stand-alone discovery, so I do not press it as my preferred configuration. I keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B013 (optical lattice clocks) first as the clearest case of a measurement technique opening new science, with experimentally demonstrated systematics and a well-reproduced result, and ranks B014 eighth because of the unsettled superconducting mechanism and reproducibility.
responses.response: I share your preference for experimental demonstration with measured systematics, and I ranked B013 only sixth for a different reason than you might expect: I am not worried about the experiment, but about the overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and how Ye's role is separated from that earlier recognition. If the committee can show that the lattice-clock contribution is distinct, I would be willing to move it up. For B014, I would answer that reproducibility of the existence of the phases is not in doubt, while the mechanism is a separate matter.

uncertainties: Historical priority between Eva Y. Andrei's early STM flat-band evidence and the 2018 transport discovery, and whether Yuan Cao's role changes the credited set.
Whether the unresolved superconducting pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder make the committee feel B014 is too young.
Whether B013 can be shown to be distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize.
For B041, how the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 2D versus 3D split (Molenkamp versus Hasan) should be resolved, and its overlap with the 2016 prize.
I have recalled author lists and dates from memory and they should be checked against the primary literature.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile with any shortlisted candidate or credited person. I note for transparency that Eva Y. Andrei (credited on B014 but not in my proposed trio) shares my first name but I know of no relationship, and that my colleague Goran Johansson is at Chalmers Physics and has declared closeness to the circuit QED community (B046); that is his to weigh, not mine.
